## What this package is

`SummarizedExperiment7` is an **experimental** reimplementation of the
`SummarizedExperiment`/`RangedSummarizedExperiment` data structures using
the `S7` object system instead of Bioconductor's S4 classes.

Two things make this package unusual, and worth stating plainly before using it:

- **It was written agentically.** The class contracts, accessors,
  validators, and tests were produced by an AI coding agent working from a
  specification document rather than hand-written line by line by a
  human. The code has been reviewed and exercised, but it has not had the
  years of production use that the Bioconductor S4 `SummarizedExperiment`
  has had.
- **It targets a specification, not the S4 source.** Rather than porting
  Bioconductor's S4 implementation, this package was built to conform to
  [biocspec](https://github.com/biocspec)'s language-agnostic specification for `SummarizedExperiment`
  (`SummarizedExperiment-specification.md`). That specification describes
  the *contract* -- what a constructor, accessor, or combining operation
  must guarantee -- independent of R, S4, or any particular language's
  object system. biocspec also ships a formal conformance test suite
  (`summarized_experiment_conformance.yaml`); this package includes an
  adapted runner for it (`inst/conformance/run_conformance_se7.R`)
  covering the cases that are in scope for its API (see below).

Treat this package as a demonstration that a biocspec-conformant
`SummarizedExperiment` can be built outside of S4, not as a drop-in
replacement for the Bioconductor class.

## Deliberate differences from the S4 original

A handful of S4 behaviors are intentionally not replicated, because they
are implementation details rather than requirements of the biocspec
contract:

- No automatic class promotion/demotion when assigning to `rowRanges<-`;
  use `toRangedSummarizedExperiment7()`/`toSummarizedExperiment7()`
  instead.
- No `withDimnames=`/`checkDimnames=` constructor and accessor arguments.
- No `combineRows()`/`combineCols()` with fill values, no range-algebra
  delegation (`shift()`, `subsetByOverlaps()`, ...), no `seqinfo()`
  pruning.

These are documented in the relevant `R/` source files and reflected in
the conformance runner's "out of scope" list.

## Converting a real Bioconductor object: the `airway` example

The most common way to get data into `SummarizedExperiment7` from
existing Bioconductor workflows is `asSummarizedExperiment7()`, which
takes a real S4 `SummarizedExperiment`/`RangedSummarizedExperiment` and
builds its S7 equivalent by reading off `assays()`, `rowRanges()`,
`colData()`, and `metadata()`. This is a one-way, read-only snapshot --
the result is not linked back to the original S4 object.

```{r setup}
library(SummarizedExperiment7)
```

```{r airway, eval = requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE)}
data(airway, package = "airway")
airway

se7 <- asSummarizedExperiment7(airway)
se7
class(se7)
dim(se7)
```

The S7 object exposes the same core information through this package's
own accessors:

```{r accessors, eval = requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE)}
assayNames7(se7)
head(assay7(se7, "counts")[, 1:3])
head(colData7(se7))
rowRanges7(se7)
```

Because `airway` is a `RangedSummarizedExperiment`, `asSummarizedExperiment7()`
produced a `RangedSummarizedExperiment7`, whose per-feature identity comes
from `rowRanges7()` (a real `GRanges`) rather than an independent
`rowData`/`rowNames` pair:

```{r ranged, eval = requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE)}
is(se7, "RangedSummarizedExperiment7")
names(se7)[1:3]
```

Ordinary `SummarizedExperiment7` operations -- subsetting, `rbind()`,
`cbind()` -- work on the result exactly as they would on an object built
directly with `SummarizedExperiment7()`/`RangedSummarizedExperiment7()`:

```{r subset, eval = requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE)}
se7[1:5, 1:2]
```

## What `asSummarizedExperiment7()` is not

`asSummarizedExperiment7()` converts *from* the S4 world *into* this
package. It is a different operation from
`toSummarizedExperiment7()`/`toRangedSummarizedExperiment7()`, which move
between this package's own two S7 classes and will error if given an S4
object -- see their documentation for details. There is no S7-to-S4
inverse in this package.

## Comparison to Bioconductor's own S7 migration

Bioconductor's `SummarizedExperiment` package has its own in-progress S7
migration, developed on the `s7-migration` branch of
[lawremi/SummarizedExperiment](https://github.com/lawremi/SummarizedExperiment/tree/s7-migration).
It is worth being explicit about how that effort differs from this
package, since both use S7 to represent the same data structure but for
different purposes.

That branch migrates the *actual* Bioconductor package to be built on
S7 internally, while remaining a fully backward-compatible S4 object for
the roughly one thousand Bioconductor packages that depend on
`SummarizedExperiment`'s S4 API. Concretely: its core object is
constructed via `new_object(S7_object(), NAMES=..., elementMetadata=...,
colData=..., assays=..., metadata=...)` and then wrapped into a real S4
object by `new_SummarizedExperiment()`; every S7 generic (`rowData`,
`colData`, `assays`, `assay`, `assayNames`, and their setters) is also
registered as a formal S4 generic via a `setS4Generic()` helper, so
existing `setMethod()`-based extensions in dependent packages keep
working untouched. It retains the complete production feature set:
`withDimnames=`/`checkDimnames=` arguments, `GenomicRanges`/
`DelayedArray`/`HDF5Array`/`Seqinfo` integration, `findOverlaps()`/
`nearest()`/`coverage()` methods, and the various
`makeSummarizedExperimentFrom*()` constructors.

`SummarizedExperiment7`, by contrast, is a small, standalone S7 class
hierarchy with no S4 inheritance and no S4/S7 bridging. It was built to
satisfy biocspec's language-agnostic contract rather than to be a
drop-in replacement, and it deliberately omits the production features
listed above (see "Deliberate differences from the S4 original").
Its accessors are namespaced (`assay7()`, `colData7()`, ...)
specifically so they never collide with the real package's API.

| | `SummarizedExperiment7` (this package) | `lawremi/SummarizedExperiment@s7-migration` |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Demonstrate a biocspec-conformant SE built from scratch in S7 | Migrate the real Bioconductor package's internals to S7 |
| Relationship to S4 | None -- pure S7, no S4 classes involved | Dual-natured: an S7 object wrapped as a real S4 object (`new_SummarizedExperiment()`) |
| Backward compatibility | Not applicable -- new, namespaced API (`assay7()`, `colData7()`, ...) | Required -- every S7 generic is also registered as an S4 generic (`setS4Generic()`) so dependent packages' `setMethod()`s keep working |
| `withDimnames=`/`checkDimnames=` | Not implemented | Implemented |
| Range algebra (`shift()`, `subsetByOverlaps()`, `findOverlaps()`, `nearest()`, `coverage()`) | Not implemented | Implemented |
| `DelayedArray`/`HDF5Array`/`Seqinfo` integration | Not implemented | Implemented |
| `combineRows()`/`combineCols()` with fill | Not implemented | Not shown to be ported yet in the reviewed branch |
| `rbind()` merges `colData` columns across objects | Yes (fixed this session; matches the real package's `.cbind.DataFrame(args, colData, "colData")`) | Yes |
| `cbind()` merges `rowRanges` `mcols()` across objects | Yes (fixed this session) | Yes |
| `cbind()` rejects mismatched range coordinates, not just names/length | Yes (fixed this session) | Yes (`.compare(lapply(args, rowRanges), TRUE)`) |
| Code size (core class files) | ~3 files, a few hundred lines | ~2100 lines across `SummarizedExperiment-class.R`, `Assays-class.R`, `RangedSummarizedExperiment-class.R` alone |
| S7 version required | Any released S7 (CRAN 0.2.2 tested) | An unreleased S7 fork/branch -- `R/acompat.R`/`R/Assays-class.R` call an `S4_contains()` helper and pass an S4 `classRepresentation` to `S7::new_class(parent=)`, neither of which CRAN S7 0.2.2 supports |
| biocspec conformance suite applied | Yes, 16/16 in-scope cases pass (`inst/conformance/run_conformance_se7.R`) | Not executable against this branch -- see below (reviewed by reading source instead) |

Three of the real defects fixed in this package during development
(`rbind()` only keeping the first object's `colData` columns, `cbind()`
not merging `rowRanges` `mcols()`, and `cbind()`'s range-compatibility
check only comparing names/length instead of actual coordinates) turned
out to match exactly how the canonical Bioconductor S7 migration
implements the same three operations -- useful independent validation
that the fixes were in the right direction.

### Identifying and installing the matching S7 fork

`lawremi/SummarizedExperiment@s7-migration`'s most recent commit at the
time of writing (`f0689b1`, 2026-06-20 15:27:08 -0700) is titled "sync
with S7 branch API changes," confirming it tracks an unreleased S7
branch rather than a CRAN release. That branch turned out to be
[RConsortium/S7@s4-extends-s7-compat-fixes](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/tree/s4-extends-s7-compat-fixes).
(Checked first: lawremi's own fork of S7, `lawremi/S7@local_fixes`,
which is older, 2024-era, and does not have the features `acompat.R`
needs.) The tip of that branch at the time of writing,
`c582779b4aa8cd1b50c4ca45e1e9b1083d342e04` ("Reduce S4 compatibility
test duplication," 2026-06-25, version `0.2.2.9000`), was installed
over the previously installed CRAN S7 0.2.2 and does supply the
`S4_contains()` helper and S4-`classRepresentation`-as-`parent` support
that `s7-migration`'s `R/acompat.R` needs -- but with it installed,
`lawremi/SummarizedExperiment@s7-migration` still fails to load, now at
`R/Assays-class.R`: `Error in S4_contains(class): S4 classes can not
extend abstract S7 classes.` (`Assays` is declared
`new_class(..., abstract = TRUE)` and then run through
`setS4Class()`/`S4_contains()`.)

That restriction was added to the S7 branch by commit `02a5348`
("Fix S4 bridge review findings," 2026-06-24 09:14:37 -0400) and has
held unchanged through `c582779` (the tip). The commit that originally
introduced `S4_contains()`, `e75b66b` (2026-06-20 14:58:46 -0700), and
the next one after it, `abf31be` ("fix regression from introduction of
external generics," 2026-06-20 15:26:01 -0700 -- by Michael Lawrence,
just 67 seconds before `s7-migration`'s own sync commit, and almost
certainly the actual commit it was synced against), both predate that
restriction -- but neither installs into a loadable package on its own
(`R CMD INSTALL` succeeds, but the freshly installed package fails
`.onLoad` with `no applicable method for` `` `@` `` `` applied to an
object of class "S7_S3_class"` ``), because the S7 branch was mid-way
through a larger internal refactor ("massive simplification" of its
S3/S4 class representation, commit `67e88ae`) at that exact point in
its history. In other words: there is no commit of
`RConsortium/S7@s4-extends-s7-compat-fixes` that is *both* installable
and compatible with `s7-migration`'s current `Assays-class.R` -- the
window where `S4_contains()` existed without the abstract-class
restriction was also a window where the package itself didn't load.
This is a real, present incompatibility between the two branches at
their respective current tips, not a mistake in fork selection; S7's
own installed copy was left at the loadable, restriction-bearing
`c582779`, since that is what `SummarizedExperiment7` itself was
verified against (below).

Installing `c582779` also surfaced and fixed two latent bugs in
`SummarizedExperiment7` itself: that commit's revised method-dispatch
mechanism represents `rbind`/`cbind`/`` `[` `` as non-function
`S7_external_generic` sentinel objects in a package's namespace
(instead of literally re-binding base's own closures there, as CRAN S7
0.2.2 did), and two internal helpers (`assays7_bind()` in
`R/01-assays.R`, `table_rbind()` in `R/00-table-helpers.R`) had passed
the bare symbol to `do.call()`, which fetches the binding directly and
received the inert sentinel rather than a usable function. Both now
call `base::rbind()`/`base::cbind()`/`` base::`[` `` explicitly. This
also happens to be what resolves the ".Internal calls in cbind/rbind"
`R CMD check` WARNING noted elsewhere in this vignette's development
history -- the newer S7 fork's sentinel-based dispatch no longer
exposes literal `.Internal()`-calling closures under those names.

Because `s7-migration` cannot currently be loaded under any installable
S7 commit found, the biocspec conformance comparison in the table above
is based on reading its source (`R/SummarizedExperiment-class.R`,
`R/Assays-class.R`, `R/RangedSummarizedExperiment-class.R`), not on
executing its own test suite or the conformance runner against it.

As a check that the `base::`-qualified fix above is not itself a
regression, `SummarizedExperiment7` was also re-verified with the S7
fork uninstalled and the released CRAN S7 0.2.2 reinstalled in its
place: the same 62/62 testthat tests and 16/16 in-scope conformance
cases pass, and `R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual` returns to exactly
the pre-fork state of 1 WARNING (the inherent `.Internal()` call in
`cbind`/`rbind`, specific to CRAN S7 0.2.2's dispatch mechanism) + 1
NOTE. The `base::` qualification is therefore safe under both S7
versions; the S7 fork was then reinstalled to match the rest of this
section.
